transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Monterey Health), Priya Shah (Head of AI), Mark Douglas (Infrastructure), Sofia Turner (Product)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood's Model Catalog, focusing on selecting open models for Monterey's patient triage assistant, discussion of benchmark numbers (latency/cost/throughput), and compatibility matrix for hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) deployments. Customer is interested in pilot for 2-4 weeks to validate latency and cost on their sample prompts; security questions (KMS, SOC2, SSO) called out.

Topics:
- Model selection for clinical triage (safety and hallucination risk)
- Benchmarks: p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost/unit
- Compatibility: quantization, GPU/CPU profiles, KV cache and seq len support
- Deployment modes: hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
00:00 Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alyssa from Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Today we'll walk through the model catalog, show how we pick open models, our benchmark sheets, and the compatibility matrix across deployment modes.
00:28 Jordan: Great thanks, we have about 45 minutes. We're specifically interested in pickin' a base model for patient triage, low hallucination, and sub-200ms p95 if possible, but cost is obviously a concern.
00:45 Diego: Yep, understood. Quick note - p95 at sub-200 on short sequences is doable on dedicated capacity but it depends on model size and quantization. For hosted we typically see higher variance, but we've got verified performance profiles in the catalog.
01:12 Priya: When you say "verified" - do you mean you actually run the model on your infra and publish numbers? Or are these vendor reported?
01:22 Alyssa: We run our own benchmarks. The model catalog has per-model entries: throughput, p50/p95/p99 numbers, tokens/sec, and recommended quantization and batch configs. We'll share the sheet after. Diego, can you pull up the catalog?
01:38 Diego: Yep, sharing my screen - link to model-catalog.pdf in the chat. (shared link) So here is the catalog view. Note that some names may be off in the transcript because of auto-transcribe - e.g., we call our feature Redwood Optimize in the console.
02:05 Diego: On the left you see model families - open models we curate (LlamaX-13B, Omega-7B, Pegasus-2) - these are examples - each entry has bench runs on NVIDA A100 and H100 and also CPU fallback. We tag models by recommended usage: instruction-following, summarization, embeddings, etc.
02:40 Mark: Sorry - H100? We're running on-prem with mixed infra and want to know compatibility with our A40s and some CPUs for fallbacks.
02:51 Diego: Right - compatibility matrix includes GPU support and the kernel selection logic. For A40s we have performance profiles (quant profiles) but H100s obviously faster. Catalog includes quantization recommendations: int8, awq, and bitsandbytes 4-bit profiles where supported. There are some edge cases on seq length - long context models keep KV caches and need memory tuning.
03:22 Jordan: On hallucinations - how do you recommend models? We don't want a model that makes confident but incorrect clinical assertions.
03:34 Alyssa: Good question. The catalog ranks models not just by perf but by quality for certain tasks - we have evaluation harness results for safety and factuality for clinical prompts. Those are tied to prompt eval sets. We can run your sample prompts to produce regression metrics.
04:02 Priya: Perfect. We'll send a 20-30 prompt set - mix of triage, diagnosis clarifiers, and follow-up questions.
04:12 Diego: Awesome. For the pilot we usually do three model variants: a smaller fast model (7B quantized), a balanced 13B, and one larger where needed. That lets you see latency/cost tradeoffs quickly.
04:30 Sofia: Do you have an example compatibility matrix? Like, if we pick LlamaX-13B quantized to 4-bit, does that run on A40s?
04:42 Diego: For A40s it's usually fine with 4-bit codecs but there may be additional memory pressure - our matrix flags recommended batch sizes and slab allocations. I'll include an exported matrix as CSV in the follow-up.
05:05 Jordan: Talk to me about hosted vs dedicated vs private. Our security team leans to VPC/private due to PHI concerns.
05:18 Alyssa: Sure. Hosted is fastest to get started (API keys, no infra setup). Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with SLA and consistent p95 - good if you want predictability. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you the control and network isolation for PHI; we run a customer-managed control plane and offer KMS/HSM integrations for key custody. Diego can go deeper here.
05:44 Diego: Just a quick caveat - private deployments require some infra checklist: supported GPU drivers, container runtime, and networking ports for control plane. We do provide an on-prem package. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, or customer's HSM. Audit logs are exported to your SIEM.
06:15 Mark: Ok our infra folks will want that checklist. Can you provide one?
06:21 Alyssa: Yes, we'll send the infra checklist and SOC2 docs.
06:26 Jordan: What about data retention and logs? We can't have logs with patient PII stored outside.
06:33 Diego: For Private or Dedicated we can disable logging or keep logs only within your VPC. Hosted has configurable retention and you can opt-out; for PHI we usually do private or dedicated so logs and KV cache never leave your environment.
06:55 Priya: Bench numbers - can you show an example where you compare cost per 1k tokens across models?
07:06 Diego: Sure. Here's a bench row - LlamaX-7B quantized gives ~1200 tokens/sec on A100 and p95 ~180ms at batch 1, cost estimate X; LlamaX-13B quantized is ~650 tokens/sec, p95 ~260ms; larger 30B is >500ms on similar infra. These are approximations - we publish the raw bench runs.
07:42 Jordan: Those p95s matter. For triage we have short prompts with 150 tokens responses usually. If we see 180ms p95 that seems okay.
07:55 Diego: Exactly. Also consider caching - for repeated prefixes we can reduce token cost and latency using prefix/KV caching in Redwood Optimize.
08:15 Sofia: Is KV cache supported in Private?
08:19 Diego: Yes, KV cache is supported in all deployment modes but cache placement differs: hosted cache lives in our managed layer, dedicated has isolated cache per customer, and private keeps cache in your environment. We'll show config snippets in the compatibility doc.
08:41 Priya: On the catalog entries, I saw some model names that are slightly off - is that because they're community forks?
08:47 Alyssa: Yes, we include community variants and forks; we label provenance (HF card, repo). Some transcription may mislabel names, sorry.
08:58 Jordan: Do you allow pinning model versions and rollout strategies?
09:03 Diego: Yes - pin model version in route configs, and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to a smaller model. Observability traces token-level cost and latency and you can set alerts on quality regressions.
09:27 Mark: Will your observability integrate into our Datadog?
09:31 Diego: Yep we have exporters, and logs/metrics can be forwarded via API/OTel.
09:36 Priya: Any limits on function calling or structured output? We have structured triage forms to fill out.
09:44 Alyssa: The catalog flags models that perform better on structured SFT tasks; we also provide function/tool calling support in the API and JSON schema enforcement to reduce hallucinations.
10:05 Jordan: Regarding quantization and quality - is there an evaluation matrix that shows quality delta when going from 16-bit to 4-bit?
10:15 Diego: We include quality-at-quantization plots in the bench sheet - they show BLEU/ROUGE-style deltas for tasks we tested and also our regression tests for hallucination rates. Results vary by model; some 7B models hold up well under 4-bit, others degrade.
10:38 Priya: Can you run our triage prompts under the same quant configs?
10:42 Diego: Absolutely - that's part of the pilot. We'll run your 20-30 prompt set across the three model variants and return p95/p50, cost/1k tokens, and a small quality score.
11:03 Sofia: One more on deployment: if we start hosted to iterate, can we flip to private later without rewiring code?
11:11 Alyssa: Yes - our deployment abstraction is intended to be transparent. You can pin routes to different backends, and the API/SDK remains the same. There are config differences (auth, networking) but no major code changes.
11:33 Jordan: Good. Do you have customers in healthcare doing PHI workloads?
11:38 Alyssa: Yes we have a couple of customers on Dedicated and Private configs for regulated data. We'll redact names in the doc but include case studies and compliance references.
11:51 Priya: On SSO, we need SAML + SCIM provisioning.
11:56 Diego: We support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC.
12:02 Mark: Any network egress concerns for private?
12:06 Diego: Private keeps control plane ops minimal; data does not egress if configured. We'll include exact network ports in the infra checklist.
12:21 Jordan: Ok let's talk about success criteria for the pilot - what should we measure?
12:27 Priya: For us: latency p95 under 300ms for the balanced model, hallucination rate under X% (we'll define), and cost per session under $Y.
12:36 Alyssa: Sounds good. We'll help define those and run bench runs against your sample. We'll also suggest batching and quantization knobs in Redwood Optimize to hit targets.
12:50 Diego: I'll also include recommended autoscale config for Dedicated so you get predictable throughput.
13:02 Sofia: What about model updates - if a community model patches weights, how do you handle rolling them out?
13:09 Diego: We treat model versions as immutable in the catalog; updates create a new version so you can roll forward and test via canary before full promotion.
13:22 Jordan: Any legal language we should be aware of? Liability, IP?
13:27 Alyssa: We'll send the standard enterprise terms; for models we indicate provenance and whether license requires attribution. Legal can review model license constraints.
13:40 Priya: Ok timeline - we want to kick off pilot next week if possible.
13:45 Alyssa: We can kick off a lightweight bench this week if you provide prompts and some infra details. For a private deploy it'll take longer - typically 3-6 weeks for full private setup.
14:02 Jordan: Good. Next steps recap?
14:04 Alyssa: We'll send model catalog PDF, bench spreadsheet, infra checklist, SOC2/KMS docs, and a CSV compatibility matrix. You'll send prompts and target metrics. We'll schedule a pilot kickoff.
14:20 Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
14:25 Mark: Thanks.

(occasional crosstalk and small microphone adjustment sounds; transcription has some mis-hearings on model names and product features)

End of transcript.
